text: The pipeline begins with an input referring expression describing specific fine-grained visual attributes.
Alongside the text, a query image containing multiple candidate objects is provided.
Both inputs pass through a shared backbone and feature enhancer to extract cross-modality representations.
Next, the Contextual Attribute Density Generate Module computes attribute-specific density representations.
Multi-scale visual features are extracted across four distinct resolution levels.
Simultaneously, the corresponding text feature is extracted for the referring expression.
A linear projection layer maps the visual features into the text embedding space.
The active text query is selected to align with the visual representations.
Element-wise multiplication calculates the cross-modal similarity.
This produces similarity features highlighting regions relevant to the expression.
The similarity and visual features are fed into a U-shape estimator to predict attribute density.
The estimator outputs predicted contextual attribute density maps.
Ground truth density maps provide direct contextual supervision.
A density loss optimizes the estimator to accurately capture attribute intensity.
Intermediate representations from the estimator form multi-scale contextual attribute density features.
These features then enter the CAD Attention Module to enrich visual representations.
The module first applies spatial attention to emphasize target foreground regions.
The multi-scale density features serve as inputs to the spatial attention branch.
Two-dimensional max pooling is performed across the channel dimension.
Simultaneously, average pooling aggregates channel information.
The pooled descriptors are concatenated along the channel axis.
A convolutional layer processes the combined feature maps.
A sigmoid activation produces the spatial attention map.
Following spatial attention, channel attention is applied to enhance category discriminability.
The primary visual features are brought into the channel attention block.
They are weighted by the spatial attention map to yield spatially attended features.
Max pooling is computed across spatial dimensions.
Average pooling also summarizes spatial statistics.
Both vectors are processed through a shared multi-layer perceptron.
The resulting channel features are merged via element-wise addition.
A sigmoid function generates the final channel attention weights.
The channel weights modulate the spatially attended features.
This produces the final CAD-enhanced visual features.
In parallel, the CAD Dynamic Query Module initializes expressive object queries.
The density initialization branch incorporates visual density priors.
Multi-scale CAD features provide image-specific density cues.
The top K density positions with highest similarity scores are selected.
The text initialization branch constructs text-dynamic queries.
The text feature vector is projected through linear and GELU activation layers.
Initial query embeddings interact with the dynamic text representations.
Matrix multiplication computes dynamic text weights across query tokens.
These weights re-modulate the text features into text-dynamic queries.
Cross-attention fuses the text-dynamic queries with the top K density features.
This produces highly distinctive dynamic queries.
The dynamic queries, CAD-enhanced visual features, and text features are gathered.
They are fed into the cross-modality localization decoder to refine query positions layer by layer.
The decoder outputs bounding box predictions and counts for the referred objects.
Finally, the model is trained end-to-end with the combined localization and density loss.
